title: D-One Adapter Dry-Run Plan
description: Deterministic dry-run plan written by scripts/done_image_adapter.py. The plan records the validated D-One generation requests for a future generator to consume. The plan is NOT D-One integration — no D-One call is made and no image bytes are produced. The schema is strict on shape and on the dry-run sentinel fields (mode, note, manifest_source); deeper safety gates (no URLs / credentials / source-text leakage / full-slide wording in prompts; ids resolve in image_manifest.json; manifest_source matches manifest entry) are enforced by scripts/done_image_adapter.py at write time and re-runnable via `done_image_adapter.py --validate-plan`. Optional per-request taxonomy fields (rendering_style / palette_family / image_role / layout_pattern / modifier / text_policy / subject_domain — seven dimensions total) may appear ONLY when the caller passed `--descriptor-vocabulary <path-to-d_one_descriptor_vocabulary.json>`; the runtime then refuses any taxonomy value not in the matching image_taxonomy.<dim>.allowed_values list, and `--validate-plan` re-runs the same vocabulary check whenever the plan carries taxonomy fields. An additional optional per-request `custom_descriptor` escape hatch may also appear when the caller passed `--descriptor-vocabulary`; the runtime refuses any value not present in the vocabulary's `custom_descriptors[*].value` allow-list.

schema_version.description: Plan-file schema version. Locked to integer 3 today. Bumped only with a paired script change so a future real-D-One generator can refuse a plan shape it does not recognize. The 1 -> 2 bump was the paired change for the optional per-request taxonomy fields (rendering_style / palette_family / image_role / layout_pattern / modifier / text_policy / subject_domain). The 2 -> 3 bump is the paired change for the new optional per-request `custom_descriptor` escape-hatch field: an older reader with schema_version=2 would reject that property under the per-request additionalProperties:false lock, so the shape change is not backward-compatible and gets a new version. Plan files without `custom_descriptor` written by a current writer still ship with schema_version=3 — the version reflects the schema shape, not the per-request payload.

mode.description: Evidence the plan was produced by the adapter stub — no D-One call was made and no image bytes were generated. The enum lock is the dry-run gate: a 'type: string' alone would silently accept 'live' / 'production' / arbitrary strings; a future real-D-One mode must bump schema_version and extend this enum (a paired change).

note.description: Self-describing audit note. Must contain the literal 'D-One adapter contract stub' so the file is identifiable as stub output even when read out of context.

request_count.description: Equal to len(requests). Redundant with the array length but kept so a glance at the file shows the count without parsing the array. The adapter cross-checks the equality before writing.

id.description: Asset id. Must match an images[].id in the workspace's image_manifest.json whose source == 'd_one_local'. The cross-check (done_image_adapter --validate-plan / write-time validate) refuses unknown ids and duplicates.

prompt.description: Safety-scrubbed prompt. The adapter has already run the defense-in-depth deny list (URIs / file paths / raw-source markers / 40-char source shingles / credential and PII shapes / full-slide-page-screenshot wording / public-distribution wording — 'upload to public' / 'public upload' / 'share publicly' / 'public hosting' / 'publish to web' / 'public url' / 'public link' / 'public cdn' / 'host publicly' and the documented variants) against this string before the plan was written; --validate-plan re-runs the same scan.

manifest_local_path.description: Workspace-relative local_path copied verbatim from the matching images[].local_path. The schema enforces non-empty string; the cross-check enforces local_path_is_safe (no URI / no leading '/' / no '..' segment) and _resolves_within against the workspace, and that the value equals the manifest entry's local_path byte-for-byte.

manifest_source.description: Always 'd_one_local'. local_asset / synthetic manifest entries are not eligible for D-One generation and the adapter refuses to issue requests against them; the enum lock is the schema-level reflection of that rule.

intended_use.description: Optional. Short caller-supplied descriptor (e.g. 'spot illustration'). Must not contain full-slide / page / screenshot wording — the adapter and --validate-plan both re-scan this field.

width_px.description: Optional. Target asset width in pixels. Positive integer.

height_px.description: Optional. Target asset height in pixels. Positive integer.

rendering_style.description: Optional. Clean-room rendering-style taxonomy token (dimension 1 of image_taxonomy in d_one_descriptor_vocabulary.schema.json). May appear ONLY when the writer / validator passed `--descriptor-vocabulary <path>`. Two layers gate this field, in this order: (1) the runtime allowed_values cross-check in scripts/done_image_adapter.py runs FIRST against the in-memory spec (and at --validate-plan time against the parsed plan), refusing any value not in image_taxonomy.rendering_style.allowed_values BEFORE the plan file is written; (2) the pattern lock on this property — which mirrors the descriptor-vocabulary's lowercase-identifier positive whitelist + forbidden-token deny clause (refuses 'public', 'upload', 'raw', 'customer', 'confidential', 'screenshot', 'credential', 'password', 'secret' as bounded tokens, and the compound phrases 'full slide' / 'image search' / 'web generation' / 'page generation' / 'slide generation' across any '.' / '_' / '-' separator stacking) — is a post-write defense-in-depth gate: the writer runs _schema_validate on the just-written plan after the runtime check, so an unsafe value that somehow slipped past the runtime gate (e.g. a future refactor loosened the runtime check, or a hand-authored plan bypassed the writer entirely) is still caught by this pattern when --validate-plan is run.

palette_family.description: Optional. Clean-room palette-family taxonomy token (dimension 2 of image_taxonomy). Same gating, pattern lock, and runtime allowed_values check as rendering_style.

image_role.description: Optional. Clean-room image-role taxonomy token (dimension 3 of image_taxonomy). Same gating, pattern lock, and runtime allowed_values check as rendering_style.

layout_pattern.description: Optional. Clean-room layout-pattern taxonomy token (dimension 4 of image_taxonomy). Same gating, pattern lock, and runtime allowed_values check as rendering_style.

modifier.description: Optional. Clean-room intensity / texture modifier (dimension 5 of image_taxonomy). Same gating, pattern lock, and runtime allowed_values check as rendering_style; intentionally optional, mirroring d_one_descriptor_vocabulary.image_taxonomy.modifier.

text_policy.description: Optional. Clean-room text-rendering policy (dimension 6 of image_taxonomy — e.g. 'no_text', 'decorative_glyphs', 'caption_safe'). Same gating, pattern lock, and runtime allowed_values check as rendering_style. The local pipeline never embeds source-derived prose or customer-facing language into rendered art; this field records the policy the request was made under.

subject_domain.description: Optional. Clean-room subject-domain token (dimension 7 of image_taxonomy — e.g. 'abstract_geometry', 'process_motif', 'metric_emblem', 'concept_diagram'). Same gating, pattern lock, and runtime allowed_values check as rendering_style. Deliberately NOT an industry / customer / product / brand token — the forbidden-token deny clause refuses such values at the schema layer in any case.

custom_descriptor.description: Optional. Clean-room *custom-descriptor escape hatch* — aligned only with upstream ai-image's custom rendering / palette / hero-composition direction (no upstream code, prompts, examples, assets, or wording copied). Two layers gate this field, in this order: (1) the runtime allow-list check in scripts/done_image_adapter.py runs FIRST and refuses any value not present in the supplied --descriptor-vocabulary's `custom_descriptors[*].value` list (an empty / absent list means the request layer has no escape hatch at all); (2) the pattern lock on this property mirrors the descriptor-vocabulary's lowercase-identifier positive whitelist + forbidden-token deny clause (refuses 'public', 'upload', 'raw', 'customer', 'confidential', 'screenshot', 'credential', 'password', 'secret' as bounded tokens, and the compound phrases 'full slide' / 'image search' / 'web generation' / 'page generation' / 'slide generation' across any '.' / '_' / '-' separator stacking) as a post-write defense-in-depth gate. The same full prompt safety scan the writer runs against `prompt` (URI / file-path / source-marker / source-shingle / credential / PII / full-slide / public-distribution / editable-text and — under text_policy='no_text' — visible-text wording) is also re-applied to this value on BOTH the raw lowercased form AND a separator-normalized form (every run of `.` / `_` / `-` collapsed to a single space), so a compound deny-list literal NOT in the schema's closed 5-compound deny list — `slide title`, `body copy`, `render the slide`, `include text`, etc. — still fires on `slide_title` / `body-copy` / `render.the.slide` / `include_text` and every other separator stacking, closing the substring-scan gap that a pure raw-form scan would leave open. So an allow-list entry that drifted into an unsafe shape is still refused. May appear ONLY when the writer / validator passed `--descriptor-vocabulary <path>`; otherwise the runtime refuses the request before any plan file is written.
